package_info.package_name: Dridex (macOS variant via malicious Word document)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware delivered via malicious document, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (variant targeting macOS, distributed via malicious Word documents)
package_info.why_malicious: The Dridex banking malware is delivered through Word documents containing auto-open macros that execute malicious code as soon as the document is opened, targeting macOS users. This behavior is explicitly designed to compromise systems and steal sensitive information without user consent.

execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro in Word document (auto-open macro)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
    ' Malicious payload here
    Call MaliciousRoutine
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open (import-time), the macro executes automatically, launching a malicious routine that may download and execute further payloads, exfiltrate data, or perform other unauthorized actions, resulting in system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Auto-open macros that execute code immediately upon document opening are a well-known vector for malware delivery, especially when the macro initiates further downloads or system modifications.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not contain macros that execute automatically and perform system-level actions without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-open macros are sometimes used in legitimate business documents for automation, but such use should never involve downloading or executing untrusted code.
key_indicators: Presence of AutoOpen or Document_Open macro
Code that initiates network connections or process execution
No user interaction required for execution

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious Word document, triggering the auto-open macro.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious payload on the macOS system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro downloads and/or executes additional malware components, such as the Dridex banking trojan.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, credential theft, or further malware installation.

behavioral_signatures: Auto-executing macros in Office documents (AutoOpen, Document_Open)
Macros that initiate network connections or download executables
Macros that attempt to execute shell commands or scripts on macOS
file_indicators: Word documents with embedded macros (especially with AutoOpen or Document_Open)
Unusual macro code in documents received from untrusted sources
network_indicators: Outbound connections from Office processes (e.g., Word) to suspicious domains or IPs
Downloads of executable payloads from macro code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents containing auto-executing macros, especially those that attempt to download or execute additional files. Use endpoint protection to block or alert on Office processes spawning child processes or making network connections. Flag documents with suspicious macro code, particularly those using AutoOpen or Document_Open routines.
